concepts.title: Character Capacity of ASCII and ISCII Codes
concepts.definition: Keyboard characters reach a computer as numeric codes: ASCII assigns 7-bit values covering 128 English characters, while the 8-bit ISCII scheme keeps those 128 codes and adds another 128 slots for Indian script symbols.
concepts.key_idea: A code of n bits can label exactly 2 raised to n different characters.
question_patterns: How many different characters can a 7-bit ASCII code represent?
ISCII uses 8 bits. How many codes does it offer in total, and how many of them are reserved for Indian script characters beyond ASCII?
Why was ASCII designed with 7 bits, and what count follows from that choice?
A new scheme uses 9 bits per character. Find how many symbols it can encode.
State the full form of ASCII and ISCII.
Letter A carries the code 65. Convert that code value into 7-bit binary.

solution_steps.explain: Each bit doubles the number of available codes.
Half of an 8-bit scheme covers the retained ASCII range.

worked_examples.q: ASCII codes characters with 7 bits. How many distinct characters can it label?

concepts.title: Positional Value in a Number System
concepts.definition: Every number system has a base equal to its count of distinct symbols, and each symbol's worth depends on its slot: the positional worth is the base raised to the slot number, counted from zero at the right of the integer part.
concepts.key_idea: Slot zero sits at the right of the integer part, and each step left raises the power of the base by one.
question_patterns: Write the base values of the binary, octal and hexadecimal systems.
A number system uses B distinct symbols. What is its base?
Find the positional worth of the digit sitting at position 3 in a base-10 number.
In the octal number (257), what power of 8 weights the leftmost digit?
Why is a number system called positional? Explain with the digits of 123.45.

solution_steps.action: raise the base to the slot number
solution_steps.explain: Slot numbers start at 0 on the right, so the worth is a power of the base.
Multiplying the symbol by its positional worth gives its share of the number.

worked_examples.q: In base 10, what is the positional worth of the third slot to the left of the decimal point?

concepts.title: Binary to Decimal Conversion
concepts.definition: A binary string names a decimal value: weight each bit by the matching power of two, counting from 1 at the rightmost bit, and add all the weighted shares together.
concepts.key_idea: Powers of two double from right to left, so each bit position is worth twice the one after it.
question_patterns: Convert (1101) into its decimal equivalent.
Express (11001010) as a base-10 number.
Find the decimal value of (1010111).
A register holds the bits 1001011. What number does a human read from it?
Add up the powers of two for the binary string 1000001 and confirm which character code it matches.

solution_steps.explain: The rightmost bit counts 1 and the next counts 2.
Remaining bits carry 4, 8, 16 and so on, doubling leftwards.

worked_examples.q: Convert the binary number 1011 to decimal.

concepts.title: Decimal to Binary by Repeated Division
concepts.definition: To rewrite a decimal number in binary, divide it by 2 over and over, jot down each remainder, stop when the quotient reaches zero, and then read the remainders from last to first.
concepts.key_idea: Remainders appear least-significant bit first, which is why the collected column is read upside down.
question_patterns: Convert (54) into binary using repeated division by 2.
Show the division steps that turn (122) into its binary form.
Convert (120) to binary and list the remainders in the order you collect them.
Why are the remainders written in reverse order at the end of a decimal-to-binary conversion?
Turn (65) into binary and verify the result by expanding powers of two.

solution_steps.explain: Dividing by 2 leaves a remainder that is the rightmost binary digit.
The quotient carries the remaining bits.
The remainder of the halved value is the second binary digit.
Continue while the quotient is still positive.
Remainders keep surfacing least-significant first.
Repeated halving walks through every bit.
Collect one remainder per division.
The remainders from last to first spell the binary numeral, here kept as a digit string.

concepts.title: Binary Grouping into Octal and Hexadecimal
concepts.definition: Because 8 and 16 are powers of two, a binary string converts to octal or hexadecimal by cutting it into chunks of 3 or 4 bits from the right and swapping each chunk for its single digit.
concepts.key_idea: Three bits make one octal digit and four bits make one hexadecimal symbol, so long bit strings shrink sharply.
question_patterns: Convert (10101100) into octal by grouping bits three at a time.
Rewrite (0110101100) as a hexadecimal number.
Why do three binary digits exactly cover one octal digit?
Write the binary equivalent of the octal number (705).
Express (23D) in binary.
Convert (1110001000) into both octal and hexadecimal.

solution_steps.explain: Weights 4, 2 and 1 turn three bits into one octal digit.
The next three bits carry the same weights in their own slot.
Shifting the high digit one decimal place appends the low digit.

worked_examples.q: How many bits are grouped to form one hexadecimal digit?

concepts.title: Hexadecimal Colour Codes for Web Pages
concepts.definition: A screen colour mixes red, green and blue, each stored as one byte, so a colour needs 24 bits; writing each byte as a two-symbol hexadecimal pair gives compact codes such as FF0000 for pure red.
concepts.key_idea: One byte per channel means 24 bits per colour, which folds into six hexadecimal symbols.
question_patterns: How many bits does a web colour need, and why?
The colour white stores 255 in each channel. Write its hexadecimal code.
A palette holds every 24-bit colour. How many colours is that?
Convert the red channel value 128 into its two hexadecimal symbols.
Why are 24-bit colour codes written in hexadecimal rather than binary?
State the hexadecimal triplet for black and justify each pair.

solution_steps.action: count the bits in the colour
solution_steps.explain: Each of the three channels takes one byte of 8 bits.
Every bit doubles the palette, so raise 2 to the bit count.

worked_examples.q: An RGB colour stores one byte each for red, green and blue. How many bits does one colour need in total?

concepts.title: Fractional Binary to Decimal
concepts.definition: Bits after the binary point carry negative powers of two: the first is one half, the next one quarter, then one eighth, and the decimal value is the sum of these fractional shares.
concepts.key_idea: Left of the point the powers of two grow; right of it they halve from one half downwards.
question_patterns: Convert (0.101) to a decimal fraction.
Find the decimal value of (100101.101).
What weight does the third bit after the binary point carry?
Express the binary fraction 0.01 as a decimal number.
Add the fractional shares of 0.111 and give the decimal total.

solution_steps.explain: The first fractional bit counts one half.
The second fractional bit counts one quarter.
The third fractional bit counts one eighth.
The fractional decimal value is the total of all weighed shares.

worked_examples.q: In fractional binary, what decimal value does the first bit after the binary point carry?

concepts.title: Unicode and UTF Encodings
concepts.definition: Unicode assigns one number to every character of every written language, so text survives across devices and programs; its UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 forms differ in how many bits each character occupies.
concepts.key_idea: Codes 0 to 128 agree with ASCII, which keeps ordinary English text unchanged under Unicode.
question_patterns: Why does one character in UTF-32 need more storage than the same character in UTF-8?
What advantage does Unicode offer when preparing digital content in an Indian language?
How does Unicode treat the first 128 codes compared with ASCII?
Name the three commonly used Unicode encoding forms.
A Devanagari letter carries the code 0905 in hexadecimal. Why can every device display it identically?

solution_steps.explain: UTF-8 uses the fewest bits for common characters, UTF-16 doubles that for many scripts, and UTF-32 always spends four bytes, so wider forms trade storage for uniformity.

worked_examples.q: Which Unicode encoding stores every character in a fixed 4 bytes?

worked_examples.title: Hexadecimal (3A5) to decimal
worked_examples.problem: Convert the hexadecimal number 3A5 into its decimal value.

steps.explain: The leftmost slot of a three-symbol hexadecimal number weighs 16 squared.
The digit 3 sits in the 256s slot.
A stands for 10, sitting in the 16s slot.
Add the weighted shares of all three symbols.

worked_examples.answer_note: The hexadecimal 3A5 evaluates to 933 in decimal.

worked_examples.title: Binary (10101100) to octal
worked_examples.problem: Convert the binary number 10101100 into octal.

steps.action: pad to a multiple of three

steps.explain: Concatenate the three decoded digits left to right.

worked_examples.answer_note: The groups 010 101 100 decode to 2, 5 and 4, so the octal form is 254.
